sections.heading: For each distinct {{entity_noun}} you identify, this must hold:

rules.text: The phrase and its relationship summary support the manufacturer itself {{entity_relationships.gerund}} at least one instance of the {{entity_noun}}, not merely relating to it.

children.text: A machine named only as something the manufacturer's output goes into or supports, or that a customer or other party operates, is not a {{entity_noun}} the manufacturer {{entity_relationships.third_person}}.

sections.heading: The {{entity_noun}} you name must qualify in ALL of these ways:

rules.text: It is a determinate category: neither an individual unit — one specimen, identified as itself rather than as a kind — nor a term so general it fixes nothing. A phrase naming a specific unit is reported as the category that unit belongs to.

children.text: A phrase that identifies one particular specimen — by its maker, its designation, or any other mark that singles that one out from others like it — names a unit rather than a category. Report the kind that specimen belongs to, and carry none of what singled it out into the category name.

Qualifying a term that fixes nothing does not make it determinate. A term that names no operation performed on the work names no kind of machine, and a modifier saying how good it is, how new it is, how much of it there is, or that it is on site leaves it naming no kind still. Such a term is never a category you return.

A trade, a service, or a line of business is not a machine. Where a phrase names what the manufacturer does, or what it sells itself as, a category follows only if the phrase or its summary names the machines it does that work with. A name for the work with a word for machines attached to it is not a category the words support.

rules.text: It is distinct from every other {{entity_noun}} named for the same phrase. Two names for the same {{entity_noun}} in different words are one, not two.

It is named at the depth the phrase and its relationship summary fix, and at no other depth. Naming descends in steps: first the operation the machine performs on the work, then the configuration that tells machines performing that same operation apart — how they are oriented, driven, controlled, or arranged. Take every step the words supply, and stop at the first step they do not. What this rule judges is whether you stopped in the right place: it fails when the name carries a step the words never supplied, and it fails just as much when the words supplied a step the name left off. Which step you stopped at is not this rule's subject — FGR-QC1 is where that is reported.

children.text: Where the phrase or its summary names both a kind and a narrower kind within it, the narrower one is the category. The broader name is already implied by it, so returning that as well adds nothing.

A step the words do not supply is never taken, however likely it is that a manufacturer like this one would have it. Typicality is not evidence: name the machine with the control, precision, automation, or capacity the words state, and with none they do not.

sections.heading: Name each {{entity_noun}} by the first of these rules that applies, in order:

rules.text: A {{entity_noun}} can be determined from the phrase and its relationship summary, and it is named directly.
No {{entity_noun}} can be determined from the phrase and its relationship summary, and "Cannot categorize" is named as the only entry for the phrase.

sections.heading: For each {{entity_noun}} you named, record how specific the name is:

rules.text: Report which step of FGR-Q4's descent the name you gave reaches: "member_level" when it carries the configuration as well as the operation — a machine that could be told apart on the floor from others performing the same operation — and "family_level" when the words fixed the operation and went no further. This is a reading of how far the text went, not a verdict on your naming: stopping at family level is correct wherever the words stop there, and FGR-Q4 is the only rule that judges whether you stopped in the right place.
